title: Phase 1 managed-dependant transition boundary
decisionSource: Product Authority steer in the governed Issue #32 baseline task
decision: Phase 1 adopts an explicit, independently testable fail-closed ownership/access transition fence. Incomplete, ambiguous, failed, or partially applied transitions must not broaden access. Advanced independent document-access transfer, complex inherited-right preservation, delegated authority chains, and enterprise entitlement transfer are deferred to a later governed capability.
question: Should Phase 1 implement managed-dependant independent-access transition semantics, retain a tested fail-closed policy fence, or remove transition representation?
evidence: REQ-P1-WS-007 preserves subject and provenance history but makes transfer conditional on an approved consent design.
WSP-P1-037 through WSP-P1-039 prohibit fabricated identity, access activation, and resource reassignment before eligibility, consent, authority and challenge rules are approved.
AC-STORY-P1-040-01 defines a safe no-transfer boundary while AC-STORY-P1-040-02 prevents completion of an executable transition without exact policy, API, reference-data and test contracts.
Architecture, Security/Privacy and Data/Domain consultation classified the missing transition semantics as a material story-local decision.

options.description: Keep Phase 1 as a tested fail-closed transition fence and defer independent-access transfer semantics to a later governed change.
impacts: Does not deliver independent-access transition in Phase 1

options.description: Define and implement complete transition semantics in Phase 1.
impacts: Broader product, legal, privacy, security, data and UX scope
Requires eligibility, consent, challenge, credential, key, grant and private-resource contracts

options.description: Remove transition representation from Phase 1 while retaining managed dependants as subjects.
impacts: Loses an explicit negative safety contract
Raises risk of later implicit transfer behavior

recommendation.reason: It preserves the approved family model while preventing sensitive authority, consent, credential, key and private-resource behavior from being invented without a complete later design.

reconciliationContinuedDuringDecision: All other hierarchy and stale-status reconciliation

futureCapability: A later governed change may add richer independent access-transfer and delegation semantics. Phase 1 must preserve extension points without implementing or implying those semantics.
